key_insight: Strain controls iodine-vacancy pair reconfiguration in CsPbI3: strong isotropic compression favors separation, tension promotes pair-preserving relay hopping, and biaxial compression produces orientation-dependent behavior.
engineering_relevance: Strain and defect orientation may offer levers for managing vacancy migration and structural stability in halide perovskites.
method: Machine-learning molecular dynamics of neighboring iodine vacancies in tilted CsPbI3.
Comparison of isotropic and biaxial strain effects on finite-temperature hopping.
Static vacancy-interaction calculations using DFT and the SevenNet-0 potential.
evidence_signal: MLMD showed nonmonotonic short-time hopping fractions with strain, while DFT and SevenNet-0 found repulsive interactions in every examined static configuration.
watch_item: Short-time hopping behavior and static interaction energies do not establish long-term vacancy-pair stability or device performance.
paper_title: Strain-dependent Dynamics of Interactions of Iodine-vacancy pairs in CsPbI3: A DFT and Machine-Learning Molecular Dynamics Study
